title: China-to-Peru Household Refrigerator Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Electromagnetic compatibility for refrigerating appliances (EN/IEC-based test scope)
rows.target_requirement: Where a Peru Reglamento Tecnico references EMC for refrigeration or power-electronic appliances, imported models should provide evidence aligned with Peru-adopted NTP test expectations for emissions and immunity, including inverter or variable-speed compressor variants. If a model includes frequency-conversion electronics, test scope and setup should be reviewed to ensure Peru-relevant conditions are covered.
target_standards: INACAL-adopted NTP clauses for electromagnetic compatibility applicable to relevant refrigerator configurations
INACAL / PRODUCE technical regulation framework where EMC is included in scope
Peru import documentation requirements for technical test evidence
rows.china_equivalent: China applies mandatory safety-EMC frameworks including GB 4343.1 and related test documents for domestic market sale under CCC. Many models are tested by GB/T or industry methods, but the report set is prepared for Chinese market conditions and accepted by Chinese authorities, not automatically by Peru import clearance.
china_standards: GB 4343.1-2018 — Emission limits and measurement methods for household appliances
GB/T 4343.2-2020 — Immunity principles for household appliances
China Compulsory Certification (CCC) process for required classes
rows.gap: The gap is typically documentation acceptance and technical scope. Chinese EMC reports must be assessed for Peru applicability and reissued or supplemented where Peru requires additional conditions, especially for inverter-based compressor designs.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where PERU technical scope for EMI/EMC applies to the imported appliance category
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory under CCC safety-EMC regime for domestic market placement in applicable classes

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] EMC evidence from China can be leveraged only after Peru scope mapping. For inverter-based refrigerators, confirm emission and immunity conditions against the Peru-applied NTP and include supplement tests where required.

rows.requirement: MTC homologación for refrigerators with radio control or connectivity modules
rows.target_requirement: If a refrigerator includes Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or other radio modules for smart-control features, the radio subsystem must satisfy Peruvian telecommunications compliance expectations and obtain MTC homologación. This includes model-level radio approval and technical data supporting permitted frequency and power behavior.
target_standards: MTC homologación requirements for radio/electronic products imported into Peru
INDECOPI product conformity process when the product class is linked to a Reglamento Tecnico
Peru import clearance checklist for communication-enabled appliances
rows.china_equivalent: China requires radio module approvals under domestic telecom and product systems (for example SRRC-related requirements) when exporting or selling communication features in China. This is separate from Peru MTC homologación and does not create automatic reciprocal recognition.
china_standards: MIIT/SRRC domestic telecom acceptance framework in China
CCC safety/EMC pathway where module is within covered appliance class
rows.gap: In Peru, an MTC step is required for connectivity-enabled refrigerators, while pure mechanical or non-radio units are not in this pathway. If a model has wireless features, test and filing scope must be separated from general electrical safety evidence and managed by the importer.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for models with radio communication modules; not mandatory for non-radio refrigerators
mandatory_status.cn: Model-dependent in China; module-specific approvals may be required domestically but are not equivalent to Peru MTC homologación

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] The safe route is: if any wireless module is present, secure Peru MTC homologación separately from the general safety/energy package. China module filings are not by themselves sufficient for Peru clearance.

source.publisher: Ministerio de Transportes y Comunicaciones (MTC), PRODUCE, and INACAL

rows.requirement: Energy efficiency and energy-labeling — MINEM requirements for refrigerators in scope
rows.target_requirement: Peru applies an energy-efficiency labeling scheme for relevant household products under MINEM. Imported refrigerators in scope require test evidence against Peru methodology, model-level energy index values in the Peruvian format, and mandatory Spanish labeling where the national rule applies. Energy data may be re-used from China only if methodology compatibility is demonstrated.
target_standards: MINEM energy-labelling program for targeted appliances
Peru technical norms adopted via INACAL and PRODUCE for refrigeration equipment in scope
Producer and importer documentation requirements for model-level Spanish labelling
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 12021.2-2015 and the China Energy Label framework for domestic sale. The Chinese class and label system is mandatory in China, but it is not a direct compliance equivalence for Peru placement, because test method, reporting format, and threshold interpretation differ.
china_standards: GB 12021.2-2015 — Minimum allowable values of energy efficiency and energy efficiency grades for household refrigerators
rows.gap: The practical gap is methodology and declaration scope: Chinese energy class is not directly mapped to Peru labelling classes without remeasurement or accepted conversion. Exporters should recalculate or test to Peru-required methodology and align manuals and label fields before customs and post-clearance audits.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the product falls under Peru energy-label scope; model evidence and Spanish labeling are required before market placement
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China under GB 12021.2 and China Energy Label for domestic sales; scope does not transfer automatically to Peru

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Energy class and label obligations are Peru-specific. Chinese GB 12021.2 and CCC energy labeling help internal quality checks but do not replace Peru evidence requirements for in-scope refrigerators.

rows.requirement: Horizontal eco-hazard and noise regimes — No direct EU-style substitute
rows.target_requirement: Peru's refrigerator compliance in this lane is primarily technical-regulation specific. There is no Peruvian regime equivalent to EU-wide RoHS-style substance bans, no blanket EU-style battery chemistry register requirement for refrigerators, and no separate EU-style outdoor-noise gate for standard indoor appliances in this compliance lane.
target_standards: INACAL and PRODUCE technical regulation framework applied by product category
INDECOPI consumer information and market surveillance rules
rows.china_equivalent: China maintains multiple environmental and electrical product systems, including CCC and China Energy Label, but these are independent from Peru's category-by-category technical clearances. For this lane, China has no direct regulatory export mirror for an EU-style horizontal RoHS or outdoor-noise compliance gate.
china_standards: No direct China-to-Peru bilateral equivalence for EU-style horizontal hazards/noise frameworks
rows.gap: Do not transfer EU-style assumptions. Exporters should avoid relying on any perceived RoHS-like or battery-hazard analogue in Peru unless a specific Peruvian law or technical norm explicitly requires it. For refrigerators, focus should remain on Peru-specific NTP adoption, MINEM labeling scope, and importer-led clearance.

mandatory_status.target: Informational in this lane — no separate mandatory Peru-wide horizontal RoHS/battery-noise regime for typical refrigerators; mandatory items remain scope-specific
mandatory_status.cn: No equivalent cross-regime in China for Peruvian import substitution of EU-style horizontal frameworks

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] The high-value gap is not a hidden RoHS-style restriction for refrigerators. For this lane, the key compliance path is Peru technical-regulation scope and market-entry documentation, plus MINEM labeling where applicable.

rows.requirement: Peru market entry and import clearance (Reglamento Tecnico, SUNAT, importer of record)
rows.target_requirement: Household refrigerators must be introduced to Peru through an importer of record established in Peru. When a category is subject to a Reglamento Tecnico, Peru import clearance at SUNAT relies on the conformity evidence package prepared by the importer and reviewed by INDECOPI/PRODUCE-related control channels. Port-of-entry practice commonly uses Callao for sea freight. The importer is the responsible local party for customs and post-clearance obligations.
target_standards: PRODUCE / INDECOPI technical regime and applicable Reglamento Tecnico framework
SUNAT import and customs clearance requirements
Port of Callao operational clearance practice for household appliances
rows.china_equivalent: China uses CCC documentation for domestic sale, import and importer-of-record responsibilities in Peru are not mirrored as a direct export clearance mechanism. Chinese certificates are evidence for Chinese market compliance and do not replace a Peru importer-led customs packet.
china_standards: CCC documentation issued by CNCA/SAMR for domestic China placement
No direct Peru-recognition mechanism for CCC under Peru customs and technical regime
rows.gap: Exporter-facing gap is structural: no CCC reciprocity and no self-clearance model in Peru. The importer must hold local registration and submit the Peru-specific packet per shipment and per product class.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for Peru placement where a Reglamento Tecnico applies and for customs release at SUNAT (Callao is a common entry point)
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for China domestic compliance via CCC; not recognized as a Peru customs substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Peru clearance for refrigerators is importer-led: work with a Peru-established importer, confirm applicable Reglamento Tecnico scope, and submit a conformity package for Callao customs. Chinese certificates support Chinese sales only.

rows.requirement: 220 V 60 Hz product adaptation and market labels (Peru vs China)
rows.target_requirement: Peru’s electrical supply context for household refrigerators is 220 V and 60 Hz. Imported products should confirm rating plate data, compressor and control settings, and instruction/manual content for this context. Spanish labeling is required where consumer laws apply.
target_standards: INDECOPI labeling and consumer information obligations (Spanish content requirements)
Peru import documentation requirements for technical adaptation
Reglamento Tecnico verification in relation to voltage-frequency operation
rows.china_equivalent: China testing for refrigerators is commonly based on 220/380 V and 50 Hz operating conditions in national certification workflows. China labeling can follow Chinese language rules and domestic naming; this does not satisfy Peru-specific labeling or voltage-frequency confirmation requirements.
china_standards: GB 4706.13-2014 and related Chinese electrical test basis
Chinese electrical supply and naming standards for domestic compliance
rows.gap: This is a practical engineering gap: not all China-tested models are immediately aligned to 220 V 60 Hz operation. Per exporter records, a model should be verified for field adaptation and updated manuals before market placement.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory operational requirement for marketable models and importer labeling responsibilities in Peru
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestic testing in Chinese conditions is separate and cannot replace Peru-specific operation/context verification

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Before release in Peru, verify Spanish labeling, voltage-frequency compatibility, and importer-led documentation alignment. 220 V 60 Hz operation is a material expectation even when China tests were done at 50 Hz.

rows.requirement: Refrigerant — R600a handling and charge documentation
rows.target_requirement: Peruvian technical requirements for imported household refrigerators generally inherit global IEC-derived safety logic on flammable refrigerants through INACAL-aligned NTP structures. R600a remains the common refrigerator refrigerant. Export models should keep clear documentation of refrigerant type, total charge, safety notices, and service guidance in Spanish where required for the market.
target_standards: INACAL-adopted NTP safety clauses for appliances using flammable refrigerants
Peru technical documentation expectations for refrigerant-bearing products
MTPE/occupational handling references where applicable to workplaces and service safety
rows.china_equivalent: China standards for household appliances include refrigerant charge safety references within GB 4706.13 and related refrigeration safety documents, including flammability considerations. China does not have a direct Peru-equivalent documentary route for Peru market clearance, so Chile-style charge values in China certificates are not automatically accepted.
china_standards: GB 4706.13-2014 and related refrigeration safety references
China Refrigeration industry practice for R600a charge controls
CCC safety certification context under CNCA/SAMR
rows.gap: The practical gap is usually documentary and model-specific. Exporters must align Peru-facing manuals and labels to include refrigerant ID and charge for the exact Peruvian configuration. Products with HFCs should be separately checked against Peru import scope and any climate-policy program applicable to refrigerants.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory to provide complete refrigerant-type and charge documentation for Peru-facing market placement, especially for flammable-media appliances
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic safety compliance under GB frameworks; not an automatic Peru clearance substitute

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] R600a is commonly acceptable in Peru-facing refrigerator programs, but Peru compliance remains documentation-driven. Confirm refrigerant declaration and charge values for each exported model in Spanish-aligned commercial and technical files.

rows.requirement: Electrical Safety — Refrigerator Safety under NTP IEC 60335-2-24
rows.target_requirement: For imported household refrigerators, Peru references INACAL-adopted NTP standards aligned with IEC 60335-2-24 and related household appliance safety provisions. INDECOPI and PRODUCE apply the relevant Reglamento Tecnico only where issued. Common requirements include insulation resistance, earth continuity, thermal cutout, enclosure strength, electrical marking, and safe use instructions for the intended supply and usage conditions.
target_standards: INACAL NTP equivalent of IEC 60335-2-24, applied through the relevant Reglamento Tecnico for refrigeration appliances
INACAL NTP IEC 60335-1 (general household appliance safety structure)
PRODUCE / INDECOPI market framework for mandatory technical regulations (Reglamentos Tecnicos)
rows.china_equivalent: China applies mandatory GB 4706.13-2014 (household and similar electrical appliances) plus GB 4706.1 as the base safety regime for domestic sale, enforced through CCC certification by SAMR/CNCA. China uses IEC lineage but maintains market-specific deviations and domestic test obligations. CNCA test/CCC records are not automatic equivalents for Peru technical regulation clearance.
china_standards: GB 4706.13-2014 — Safety of household and similar electrical appliances — Particular requirements
GB 4706.1-2005 — General requirements for household and similar electrical appliances
rows.gap: The exporter should expect Peru-focused conformity evidence in the export file set because domestic CCC dossiers are prepared for the China market. Where a Peru Reglamento Tecnico applies to refrigerators, Chinese test reports and manuals may need technical mapping and sometimes re-evaluation of electrical markings, nameplate data, and installation context under Peru importer-led clearance.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where a relevant refrigerator Reglamento Tecnico applies; conformity evidence and importer-led clearance required before Peru market placement
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China under GB 4706.13-2014 and related CCC rules for domestic sale; mandatory context differs from Peru import clearance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Domestic China CCC safety compliance is not enough on its own for Peru import placement. Exporters should map refrigerator documentation to Peru's applicable INACAL NTP-based requirements and the responsible importer should provide Peru-accepted conformity evidence under the relevant Reglamento Tecnico.
